name: ModelGain PHP Upgrade Risk Audit – PHP 8 Compatibility Checker
author: ModelGain.com

sections.description:
Your host says it is time to move to PHP 8.3, 8.4 or 8.5. The real question is: which installed plugin or theme will break when you do?

ModelGain PHP Upgrade Risk Audit is a PHP compatibility checker for WordPress. Pick the PHP version you plan to upgrade to, select the plugins and themes to inspect, and run a local static-analysis scan. Every component gets a clear verdict:

  • Ready – no known compatibility problem was found for the target PHP version.
  • Review – deprecations or warnings worth checking before or after the upgrade.
  • Blocked – code that uses functions or syntax removed in the target PHP version.
  • Incomplete – the scan could not finish, so the component is never reported as Ready by mistake.

Open any component to see the file, line, rule and message, so you or your developer know exactly what to fix or which plugin to update or replace.

Why site owners and agencies use it

  • Works on managed hosting. No exec(), shell_exec(), Composer or command-line access needed. The scanner runs inside WordPress.
  • Your code stays on your server. Nothing is uploaded to an external scanning service, so premium, custom and client plugins can be checked too.
  • Does not time out on big sites. Scans run in small AJAX batches with automatic retry, instead of one long request that hits a 500 error.
  • Read-only. The plugin never edits the code it scans and never changes your PHP version.
  • Current PHP targets. Choose any PHP 8.x target up to PHP 8.5.
  • Report you can share. The last finished report is saved on the site. Export it as CSV (spreadsheet-safe) or JSON for a client, a ticket or a change record.
  • Less noise. Findings in bundled vendor/ libraries are labeled separately from the component’s own code.

Typical workflow

  1. Before your host’s PHP deadline, open Tools → ModelGain PHP Upgrade Risk Audit.
  2. Choose the target PHP version, for example 8.4.
  3. Scan your active plugins and theme.
  4. Update, replace or ask the developer to fix anything marked Blocked.
  5. Test the upgrade on staging, then switch PHP on production.

Pro add-on for site maintainers

The free plugin stays fully functional, with no limits on what you can scan. If you maintain client sites or want to keep watching after the first audit, the optional Pro add-on adds:

  • Scheduled daily or weekly background re-scans for a target PHP version.
  • One email alert when a component newly becomes Blocked (or Review, if you choose).
  • Scan history (last 20 scans) and a comparison with the previous scan.
  • WP-CLI: wp modelgain-pua scan --target=8.4 --fail-on=blocked can stop a deployment when a component is Blocked.

Pro is $19.99 per year or $29.99 once for lifetime use, per site. It is sold through Freemius and is never required to use this plugin.

Important limitation

Static analysis can identify known PHP compatibility patterns, but it cannot execute every runtime path and cannot guarantee that a site will work perfectly after an upgrade. Always validate the final PHP change on staging before changing production.

Privacy

Scanning and scan state stay on the WordPress installation. This plugin does not upload plugin or theme source code, does not contact external services and does not include telemetry. The links to the Pro add-on page are ordinary links that only open when you click them.
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin from Plugins → Add New by searching for “ModelGain PHP Upgrade Risk Audit”, or upload the ZIP.
  2. Activate it.
  3. Go to Tools → ModelGain PHP Upgrade Risk Audit.
  4. Choose the PHP version you plan to upgrade to.
  5. Select the plugins and themes to inspect and click Scan selected components.
sections.faq:
How do I check if my plugins are compatible with PHP 8?

Install this plugin, open Tools → ModelGain PHP Upgrade Risk Audit, choose the PHP 8.x version your host offers, and scan. Components marked Blocked use code removed in that PHP version; Review means deprecations or warnings to check.

Which PHP versions can I check against?

PHP 8.0, 8.1, 8.2, 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5. The site itself can still be running PHP 7.4 or newer while you scan.

Does this change my PHP version?

No. It only analyzes source code. Changing the server PHP version remains a hosting/server operation.

Does the scanner modify plugins or themes?

No. Scans are read-only.

Does it work when shell functions are disabled?

Yes. The release package includes the scanner runtime and runs it in-process. It does not require shell execution.

Is this a replacement for the old WP Engine PHP Compatibility Checker?

It solves the same problem with a maintained rule set and current PHP 8.x targets. It is an independent ModelGain plugin and is not affiliated with WP Engine.

Can it scan premium or custom plugins?

Yes, as long as the code is installed on the WordPress site and readable by WordPress. The scan does not depend on a public compatibility database.

Does a Ready result guarantee the PHP upgrade is safe?

No. A Ready result means the static scanner did not find a known blocking pattern in the selected source. You should still test the actual upgrade on staging.

What does Incomplete mean?

The scanner could not finish a component, for example because of a PHP error during analysis or because the component contains more than 5,000 PHP files. Incomplete is never shown as Ready.

Why is ModelGain PHP Upgrade Risk Audit itself not in the component list?

The scanner deliberately excludes itself. Its bundled PHP_CodeSniffer/PHPCompatibility engine is an analysis dependency and can generate self-referential findings that do not help you assess the rest of the site.

Where is the report stored and how do I remove it?

Only the last finished report is stored, in a single non-autoloaded WordPress option on this site. It contains component names, relative file paths, line numbers and rule messages; no source code. Use Delete saved report on the tool screen, or uninstall the plugin, to remove it. Uninstall also removes it on every site of a multisite network.

Do I need Pro?

No. Every scan, verdict, report and export in this plugin is free. Pro is only for scheduled re-scans, email alerts, history/compare and WP-CLI. The small Pro card on the tool screen can be hidden with one click.
sections.changelog:
1.0.1

  • Fixed: scans started from the Tools screen could end with “Scan error” for every component on Apache/PHP-FPM sites, because the scanner engine was not loaded for each scan batch request and needed a CLI-only stream. Browser scans now work on regular web servers. A new end-to-end test runs the scan through separate admin-ajax requests.
  • Clearer plugin name, description and FAQ for people searching for a PHP 8 compatibility checker.
  • “Open audit” shortcut on the Plugins screen.
  • A small, dismissible card on the tool screen describes the optional Pro add-on. It is hidden when Pro is active. No feature of the free plugin changed or became limited.
  • Uninstall also removes the per-user “hide Pro card” preference.

1.0.0

  • The last finished report is saved on the site and shown when you return to the tool screen.
  • Export the saved report as CSV or JSON. CSV cells are protected against spreadsheet formula injection.
  • Delete saved report control; uninstall removes plugin-owned data, including on multisite.
  • New Incomplete verdict: scan errors and file-limit truncation are no longer reported as Blocked or Ready.
  • Scan batches are serialized site-wide so two tabs or two administrators cannot corrupt a scan or overload the server.
  • Automatic retry with backoff when a batch request fails because of a temporary network or server error.
  • All admin screen strings are translatable.

0.1.2

  • Packaging-only correction: exclude internal release review records from the WordPress.org install ZIP. No change to scanning behavior, stored data, settings, or upgrade identity.

0.1.1

  • Unified the public plugin name and publisher branding under ModelGain. No change to plugin slug, settings, stored data, or behavior.

0.1.0

  • Initial alpha with local plugin/theme scanning, PHP target selection, bounded processing, cancellation, and Ready / Review / Blocked results.
